classification_model.principle: One English word → one primary Chinese mapping → separate historical etymology → separate sound-semantic hypothesis → separate experimental validation.
classification_model.review_rule: LIGHT → 籁 is retained as Candidate / retain_without_promotion. The mapping, hypotheses, experiment plan, AI review and publication status are not promoted.

lifecycle.promotion_rule: AI may extract candidate records, but only documented human or research review may promote evidence level, confidence, experiment status or publication status.

sources.title: American Heritage Dictionary · language
sources.notes: Package G.2 calibration source; support boundaries are explicit.
supports: English language derives through Middle English from Old French langage, from langue, from Latin lingua.

sources.title: Middle English Dictionary · langage
sources.notes: Package G.2 calibration source; support boundaries are explicit.

sources.title: International Phonetic Association · official IPA chart
sources.notes: Package G.2 calibration source; support boundaries are explicit.
supports: /w/ is a voiced labial-velar approximant; /f/ is a voiceless labiodental fricative paired with /v/; /h/ is a voiceless glottal fricative.
does_not_support: A general W↔F/H interchange or historical sound law.

sources.title: Cambridge · Historical Linguistics / comparative method
sources.notes: Package G.2 calibration source; support boundaries are explicit.
supports: Historical sound relationships require systematic correspondence patterns rather than isolated resemblance.

sources.title: Darnell et al. · Two Early Alphabetic Inscriptions from Wadi el-Hol
sources.notes: Package G.2 calibration source; support boundaries are explicit.
supports: Early alphabetic signs in an Egyptian Middle Kingdom contact setting used acrophony from foreign sign names.
does_not_support: A proven enduring semantic value for modern Latin L.

sources.title: Höflmayer et al. · Early alphabetic writing at Tel Lachish
sources.notes: Package G.2 calibration source; support boundaries are explicit.
supports: Early alphabetic writing drew on Egyptian signs and later developed into Phoenician, from which Greek derived; chronology and some interpretations remain disputed.
does_not_support: A unique settled Egyptian pictorial source for L or a semantic law for L.

sources.title: Colless · The Origin of the Alphabet: An Examination of the Goldwasser Hypothesis
sources.notes: Package G.2 calibration source; support boundaries are explicit.
supports: A historical reconstruction connects L with Semitic lamd/lamed and Greek lambda; ox-goad is a proposed letter-name meaning.
does_not_support: Certainty about the exact Egyptian source sign; persistence of that meaning in modern English L words.

sources.title: Language Book · Advance
sources.notes: Preserves the author's mapping, segmentations, French comparisons and vance observation as author analysis rather than historical morphology.

sources.title: Cambridge Dictionary · advance (English–Chinese Simplified)
sources.notes: Bilingual lexical source with an explicit support boundary.
supports: Advance in its forward-motion sense may be translated with 前进 and, in contextual examples, 推进.
does_not_support: 往 as a unique primary translation; a historical or sound-law relation between advance/vance and 往.

sources.title: Merriam-Webster · advance
sources.notes: English word-history source with an explicit support boundary.
supports: Middle English advauncen is an alteration of avauncen, borrowed from Anglo-French avancer, ultimately from Latin abante through Vulgar Latin *abantiare.
does_not_support: ad.van.ce as historical morphology; vance as a historical adjective meaning '前的'; common origin with Chinese 往.

sources.title: Merriam-Webster · advancement
sources.notes: English and Anglo-French morphology source with an explicit support boundary.
supports: English advancement reflects Middle English avauncement, borrowed from Anglo-French avancement, formed from avancer plus -ment.
does_not_support: ad.vance.ment as the historical segmentation; vance as a free historical morpheme meaning '前的'.

sources.title: CNRTL / TLFi · avancer
sources.notes: French historical-lexicography source with an explicit support boundary.
supports: French avancer is traced to Vulgar Latin *abantiare, formed on abante.
does_not_support: A French adjective vance meaning '前的' as the historical base of avancer.

sources.title: CNRTL / TLFi · avance
sources.notes: French derivational source with an explicit support boundary.
supports: French avance is described as a deverbal noun from avancer.
does_not_support: vance as an independently established adjective meaning '前的'.

sources.title: CNRTL / TLFi · avancement
sources.notes: French derivational source with an explicit support boundary.
supports: French avancement is derived from avancer with the suffix -ment.
does_not_support: vance as an independently established adjective meaning '前的'.

sources.notes: Supports the deeper relation among Germanic light and Latin lux/lumen forms.

label.en: Possible W ↔ F/H phonetic or consonantal relation
label.zh-Hans: W ↔ F/H 的可能语音或辅音关系

statement.en: The author proposes that W may correspond with F or H in the water ↔ 哗 comparison. No regular sound change is asserted.
statement.zh-Hans: 作者提出在 water ↔ 哗 的比较中，W 可能与 F 或 H 对应；此处不声称存在已证实的规律音变。

notes.en: As stated, W and F are not a voicing pair: IPA classifies /w/ as a voiced labial-velar approximant, /f/ as a voiceless labiodental fricative (paired with /v/), and /h/ as a voiceless glottal fricative. A historical W↔F/H correspondence would require language-specific, repeated comparative data.
notes.zh-Hans: 按当前表述，W 与 F 不是清浊音对：IPA 将 /w/ 列为有声唇软腭近音，将 /f/ 列为清唇齿擦音（其浊音对应为 /v/），将 /h/ 列为清声门擦音。若主张历史上的 W↔F/H 对应，必须提供特定语言、多个词项及年代链条的比较资料。

rationale.zh-Hans: G.2 仅完成来源核验；尚未执行对象级 AI 审核。

label.en: L sound / letter L may carry an inherent semantic association

statement.en: Research whether modern L or /l/ has a repeatable semantic association across words. Historical glyph evidence is context for a separate object and does not establish this hypothesis.

notes.en: Writing-history evidence may support a historical letter name or proposed pictorial source, but it does not show that modern English /l/ or L carries that meaning across words. A separate operational semantic prediction and dataset are required.
notes.zh-Hans: 文字史资料可以支持历史字母名称或可能的图画来源，但不能证明现代英语 /l/ 音或字母 L 在不同词汇中持续携带该意义；仍需另行提出可操作的语义预测与数据集。

label.en: Historical glyph lineage associated with L / lamed / lambda

statement.en: Research the proposed path from early alphabetic signs in an Egyptian contact setting through Semitic lamed and Greek lambda to Latin L. The proposed pictorial source of lamed, often linked with an ox-goad or crook, remains a historical reconstruction—not a semantic law.
statement.zh-Hans: 研究在埃及接触环境中的早期字母符号，经闪米特 lamed、希腊 lambda 到拉丁 L 的提议路径。lamed 的图画来源常与赶牛杖或弯杖联系，但仍属于历史重建，不是语义法则。

notes.en: Sources support the Egyptian-contact context and later alphabetic transmission; the precise Egyptian sign proposed for L/lamed is not settled, and a scholarly comparison explicitly gives alternative candidates with a question mark.
notes.zh-Hans: 资料支持埃及接触背景及后续字母传播；L／lamed 所对应的具体埃及符号尚未定论，学术比较表明确以问号列出多个候选。

rationale.en: Awaiting object-level G.2 AI review.
rationale.zh-Hans: 等待 G.2 对象级 AI 审核。

label.zh-Hans: van／vance ↔ wang／往 声音—语义假说

statement.en: The author proposes testing whether van/vance and Mandarin wang/往 show a repeatable sound-semantic association around forward movement or direction. No sound change, historical correspondence, or common origin is asserted.
statement.zh-Hans: 作者提出检验 van／vance 与汉语 wang／往 是否围绕向前移动或方向形成可重复的声音—语义关联；此处不声称已证实音变、历史对应或共同词源。

notes.en: The proposal is preserved, but the historical sources explain advance through avancer and *abantiare/abante and provide no evidence for a van/vance ↔ wang/往 relation. Comparative data and a preregistered test are required.
notes.zh-Hans: 该提议已保留，但历史来源把 advance 解释为经 avancer、*abantiare／abante 演变，并未提供 van／vance ↔ wang／往 的证据；仍需比较数据与预注册检验。

chain: Latin abante (ab + ante: before / in front)

summary.en: Reliable dictionaries trace advance through Middle English and Anglo-French avancer to Vulgar Latin *abantiāre, based on Latin abante. English advancement reflects Anglo-French avancement from avancer + -ment; French avance is deverbal from avancer, and French avancement is avancer + -ment. This source-backed morphology does not contain an independently established historical morpheme vance meaning '前的'.
summary.zh-Hans: 可靠词典把 advance 经中古英语、盎格鲁法语 avancer 追溯到通俗拉丁语 *abantiāre，其基础为拉丁语 abante。英语 advancement 反映盎格鲁法语 avancement（avancer + -ment）；法语 avance 是由 avancer 逆生的名词，avancement 为 avancer + -ment。该有来源的形态分析不含一个独立且已确立、意为“前的”的历史词素 vance。

notes.en: The cited dictionary etymologies agree on the avancer → *abantiare/abante lineage and on the derivational status of avance/avancement. They do not support the author's ad.van.ce or ad.vance.ment segmentation as historical morphology.
notes.zh-Hans: 所引词典词源一致支持 avancer → *abantiare／abante 的谱系及 avance／avancement 的派生身份；它们不支持把作者的 ad.van.ce 或 ad.vance.ment 切分当作历史形态。
